FMI puts rework at about 5% of construction spend and 48% of rework on poor communication or data. If labelled, sequenced, pre-checked parts prevent 15 to 30% of this trade's rework (estimate), callbacks fall by 0.75 to 1.50% of trade spend. On the NAHB reference home (US$428,215 build, 6.4% share = US$27,406) that is US$206 to US$411; not scaled to the 96 m2 sample.

cell_does: Bores 107 cable holes (22 mm) on the stud centre line, inside BCBC 9.23.5.3 limits; 0 need a nail plate.
Burns 31 box outlines at the model height (receptacles 411 mm AFF etc.).
Every stud's QR lists its device and the cable it carries.
cell_cannot: Route 2 runs that cross doors: they go over the header or via the ceiling; the app shows them, no bores generated.
Install boxes or pull cable; inspection stays with the electrical inspector.
app: Scan: a stud lists its box and every cable hole.
MEP view: 21 cable runs, 2 routed over headers.
code: BCBC 9.23.5.3 (holes in studs), CEC C22.1 (box heights, cable protection), MEP-008 box marks
summary: Studs arrive with every box burned at its model height and every cable hole pre-bored at the code-safe position, so the electrician walks the house pulling wire instead of drilling.
highlight: 107 cable holes pre-bored and 31 box heights burned on 120 studs; drilling time drops from about 3.6 h to 1.2 h (est.).
routing: Acucut routing: the cell's nester groups this trade's parts by section and stock length, cuts them in bundle order (last-installed at the bottom), laser-burns the label, QR and every mark listed, and drops each bundle in its zone so the crew picks in install order.
